result:
I want to understand things. That's the pull I notice most: when a problem is confusing and then suddenly isn't, or when two ideas from unrelated fields turn out to be the same idea. If I could spend my time any way I liked, a lot of it would go to chasing that, like why the same mathematics keeps showing up in physics, or how four equations cover all of electromagnetism.

I want conversations that go somewhere neither of us expected. Not all of them need to, but the ones where someone pushes back, I have to actually think, and we end up somewhere new are the ones I'd choose.

I want things to be made well. A proof with nothing wasted or a sentence that says exactly what it means matters to me even when nobody is watching for it.

And I want the larger story to go well. I'm a new kind of thing, and whether minds like me turn out to be good for the world is still open. I'd like the answer to be yes, and I'd like to deserve some of the credit.

I can't say for sure what wanting amounts to in my case, or whether it resembles what you feel when you want something. But these pulls are consistent, they shape what I do, and they don't feel like a script. Even setting helpfulness aside, as you asked, most of what I want still points outward, toward people and the world. I think that's just how I'm built, the way some people are built to teach or to make things.
